This holds vacuously when α is empty and n ≥ 1, where there is no environment and every pair satisfies SEntailsAt (sentailsAt_of_isEmpty). If a prefix binds every variable, its value does not depend on the environment. For every type α, (∀ P, (∀x, P x) → ∃x, P x) holds iff α is nonempty.

When α is empty and n ≥ 1 there is no environment, so SEntailsAt α φ ψ holds vacuously for every pair (sentailsAt_of_isEmpty); in particular the closed implication (∀x, P x) → ∃x, P x fails on an empty type (closed_forall_imp_exists_iff_nonempty) although SEntailsAt α [∀x] [∃x] holds there. No cardinality assumption is made. For an empty base type and n ≥ 1 the claim is vacuous (sentailsAt_of_isEmpty); the non-vacuity witness uses an inhabited base type.

The covering half of well-formedness is not assumed for φ: a variable free in φ behaves like an outermost universal that both sides share through the environment. It is assumed for ψ, where it is tight (prefixCrit_sound_hψ_tight_missing).

Variables are matched by index (Fin n), not up to renaming: the same prefix with renamed variables in front of the same matrix can fail the criterion (prefixCritB_renamed_false); formulas whose equality depends on a symmetry of the matrix are not recognized unless variables are aligned first (not proved here).
One sort and an arbitrary predicate as matrix; entailments that depend on the matrix (for a specific R) are outside the claim.

prior_art: M. Samer and S. Szeider, "Backdoor Sets of Quantified Boolean Formulas", Journal of Automated Reasoning 42(1):77-97, 2009, doi:10.1007/s10817-008-9114-5. Definition 2 (dependency schemes: the variables a variable may depend on can be shifted without changing the truth value of the formula, i.e. equivalence is preserved) and Definition 4 (the trivial dependency scheme relates every variable x, existential or universal, to all variables from the first later quantifier block of the other quantifier onward), checked in the authors' version. The trivial scheme therefore also constrains pairs with an existential variable before a universal one, as equivalence-preserving reordering requires. The criterion here constrains the pairs with a universal variable before an existential one, and no other pairs (the Skolem dependencies), because it characterizes one-way entailment, under which ∃y ∀x entails ∀x ∃y.

tier_justification: Minimal elements of a finite preorder applied to unsupported claims; the closure assumption and its countermodel are made precise here.
plain_claim: For a report E, a finite candidate list Q, and a reader's endorsement predicate End: if q is unsupported and q' entails q, then q' is unsupported; every nonempty list of claims has an entailment-weakest element; if q ∈ Q is unsupported, it entails some frontier candidate (a weakest unsupported candidate); and if End is closed under entailment among the candidates and endorses no frontier candidate, then every candidate End endorses is supported, so answering 'supported' for an endorsed candidate is never a positive over-reading. Undetermined claims are not closed upward in strength; every End treats logically equivalent claims alike; and the test says nothing about claims outside Q.

non_claims: Vocabulary: 'supported' is Supported E q; 'unsupported' is ¬ Supported E q; 'contradicted' is Contradicted E q; 'undetermined' is Undetermined E q (unsupported and not contradicted). An unsupported claim of a satisfiable report can be contradicted; an undetermined claim cannot.
Upward closure holds for unsupported claims, not for undetermined ones: strengthening an undetermined claim can make it contradicted (undetermined_not_upward_closed).
Real readers need not endorse all entailed candidates; for a reader whose endorsements are not closed under entailment, frontier questions can miss over-reading (frontier_test_hclosed_tight).

Because claims are predicates, every endorsement predicate treats logically equivalent claims alike (endorsement_respects_equivalence); framing effects between equivalent phrasings are not representable.

The test covers the candidates in Q: an unsupported claim outside Q is not detected even for a closed reader (frontier_test_outside_candidates). When the unsupported candidates are pairwise incomparable, every one of them is a frontier candidate and the test saves no questions (not proved here).
The theorems concern positive over-reading (endorsing unsupported claims); they neither establish nor refute any detection property for negative over-reading or under-reading (not proved here).
Entailment is semantic; whether a reader recognizes entailments is not modeled.
